clue.text: Grand piano fully entertains at one toccata's conclusion

indicators.note: a host who entertains has guests inside the house, so one word holds the others

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
fully means in all respects
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: a conclusion is the end, so only the closing letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of toccata

explanation.surface: A grand piano holds the full sound as a toccata ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Grand looks like part of the phrase grand piano, but it is the definition, and the piano is just its one-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Palatial means like a palace, splendid and impressive, so a synonym for grand.

clue.text: On time, supply lines to erring actor?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to feed forgotten words to a performer from the wings

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the theatrical second sense; the first is the everyday adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for punctuality and a verb for reminding a performer of forgotten dialogue.

clue.text: Scottish boy to include in story

indicators.note: one word is placed in the middle of the other, so it sits within it

parts.note: a story can be an untruth, a fib
to include something is to add it

explanation.surface: Someone wants to write a young Scottish lad into a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Story here is a fib, not a narrative.
explanation.definitionFit: Laddie is the Scots diminutive for a young lad.

clue.text: Temperature lowered initially in America's city

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for temperature

indicators.note: in places one letter within the following word for the country

parts.note: the United States of America

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of lowered

explanation.surface: A weather report: the thermometer has dropped in a US city.
explanation.walkthrough: The L goes inside USA, after its first letter, and T stands in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa is a large city in Oklahoma, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Prepared for battle in theatre, MoD ordered choppers

indicators.note: things that are ordered are put into a new arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the ten letters of these two words, rearranged
choppers is slang for teeth

explanation.surface: The Ministry of Defence sends helicopters into a theatre of war.
explanation.walkthrough: Choppers suggests helicopters in the military surface, but it is slang for teeth; a theatre is also a zone of military operations, and MoD is Britain's Ministry of Defence.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone carrying every weapon possible, fully equipped for fighting.

clue.text: Summons to have company appearing at court?

definitions.text: Summons to have company appearing at court?

parts.words: Summons to have company appearing at court
parts.note: surface reading: a legal summons ordering a firm to appear before a judge
setter's reading: an invitation for someone to join you on a court where a racket game is played

explanation.walkthrough: Summons and court pull toward the law; the court is a sports court and the summons is a cheery call for a partner, a catchphrase of old drawing-room comedies.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock phrase is a light-hearted invitation asking whether anybody would like to play a game.

clue.text: Late shift?

parts.note: surface reading: a period of work in the evening or overnight
setter's reading: a shift is also a loose dress, and this one is worn late in the day, in bed

explanation.walkthrough: Shift reads as a work rota, but it is an old word for a simple loose dress or chemise.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment for sleeping in is a loose dress put on at the end of the day.

clue.text: Men at old port for work

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers
taken as written
O is a standard abbreviation for old
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Sailors at an old harbour looking for employment.
explanation.walkthrough: Work is the musical sense, a composition.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large musical composition for voices and orchestra, so it is an example of a work.

clue.text: Highly valued English horse touring Middle East

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: a touring party goes round a region, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: a steed is a horse
ME is the abbreviation for the Middle East

explanation.surface: A prized English horse is on tour in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: ME goes inside the horse, between its second E and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteemed means held in high regard, a synonym for highly valued.

clue.text: No longer a burning passion?

parts.note: surface reading: an enthusiasm that has cooled
setter's reading: a former lover, someone you once burned for

explanation.walkthrough: The burning imagery is literal fire as well as love: a former sweetheart is a fire that has gone out.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a past romantic partner, someone once loved but no longer.

clue.text: Gulag has twenty guards horrified

indicators.note: guards means holds within, so the answer is kept inside the run of words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Prisoners in a Soviet labour camp are appalled by their twenty guards.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast is a synonym meaning filled with shock and dismay.

clue.text: Bag grouse endlessly

indicators.note: without an end means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to grouse is to complain, to gripe

explanation.surface: A shooting party bagging grouse without end.
explanation.walkthrough: Bag and grouse suggest a day's shooting; grouse is the verb to complain, and grip is a dated word for a travelling bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A grip, short for gripsack, is a holdall or travelling case.

clue.text: Penny with hard line mad to carry on

indicators.note: mad means crazed or disordered, so the letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for penny
these eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Penny takes a tough, angry stance and keeps going.
explanation.walkthrough: Penny looks like a woman's name; it is just P. Carry on here means to have affairs, not to continue.
explanation.definitionFit: To philander is to have casual love affairs, which matches the colloquial sense of carrying on.

clue.text: Some irony from tense painter

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
a painter is a rope for tying up a boat

explanation.surface: An artist on edge speaks with a touch of irony.
explanation.walkthrough: Painter is the nautical sense, the line at a boat's bow used to moor it.
explanation.definitionFit: Irony is a figure of speech, and a trope is any such figure, so some irony is one instance.

clue.text: Carbon-free goods carried in mythical ship

indicators.note: free of something means without it, so the chemical symbol is removed

parts.note: freight carried by a ship or plane
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Freight that produces no carbon emissions travels aboard a legendary vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo carried Jason and the Argonauts in Greek legend on their quest for the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: Wife stops correcting Conservative

indicators.note: something that stops a hole sits inside it, plugging the gap

parts.note: righting a wrong is correcting it
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A wife stops putting a Tory straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Right-wing describes the political right, which in Britain is the Conservative side.

clue.text: Guarantee seaside stroll is ending in Margate

parts.note: short for promenade, a seafront walkway
taken as written

indicators.note: ending in points to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: the final letter of Margate

explanation.surface: A walk along the seafront is promised at the end of a trip to Margate.
explanation.walkthrough: Margate is a seaside resort in Kent, England; a prom is a seafront walkway.
explanation.definitionFit: A promise is a pledge, an assurance that something will happen, so a synonym for guarantee.

clue.text: See 4
Disturbed Lear isn't showing what's inside

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: these eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's mad king is not revealing his true feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrails are the internal organs, guts and innards of a body.

clue.text: Arm and leg finally shackled by barbarian

indicators.note: someone shackled is held fast by another, so these letters are held inside

parts.note: the Huns were a nomadic people, a byword for barbarians
taken as written

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of leg

explanation.surface: A barbarian has someone chained by arm and leg.
explanation.walkthrough: Arm looks like a body part next to leg, but it is the noun for a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A handgun is a firearm, and an arm is any weapon, so the gun is an example.

clue.text: Cool revolutionary beginning to feel inferior

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the preceding word is flipped

parts.note: to fan something is to cool it

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of the next word

parts.note: the opening letter of feel

explanation.surface: A trendy rebel starting to feel second-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: Cool reads as the adjective for trendy, which is ironic since the answer is British slang for uncool or tacky; here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Naff is British slang for tacky or of poor quality, so it means inferior.

clue.text: Water pipe new that blocks lavatory?

indicators.note: a thing that blocks a pipe sits inside it, so one letter goes within the word

parts.note: bog is British slang for a toilet
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A new pipe that clogs up the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: Water pipe looks like plumbing beside the lavatory, but it is a smoking device that draws smoke through water.
explanation.definitionFit: A bong is a pipe for smoking that passes smoke through water, a water pipe in that sense.

clue.text: Poorly after pong from pit comes to town

indicators.note: after places the word for poorly behind the other piece

parts.note: BO, body odour, is the smell from the armpit
feeling rough means feeling ill

explanation.surface: A sickly miner arrives in town still smelling of the pit.
explanation.walkthrough: Pit suggests a coal mine, but it is the armpit; pong is British slang for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A borough is a town with its own council, so it is a kind of town.

clue.text: I love to absorb holy book and its predecessor entirely

indicators.note: what absorbs something takes it inside, so the two books go within

parts.note: taken as written
NT is the New Testament
the Old Testament came before the New
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Someone who loves to take in the whole Bible, both testaments.
explanation.walkthrough: The I and the O together surround both testaments: I + NT + OT + O.
explanation.definitionFit: In toto is Latin for as a whole, completely.

clue.text: Commercial in which scene cut to scale

indicators.note: in which means the shortened word sits inside the commercial

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement

indicators.note: something cut is shortened, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: An advert in which a scene was edited out to fit.
explanation.walkthrough: Scale looks like a size or measure; it is the verb to climb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to climb up, the same as scaling a wall or mountain.

clue.text: Card sharp hiding nothing

indicators.note: something hiding another keeps it out of sight inside itself

parts.note: a sharp taste is tart
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A card sharp has nothing up his sleeve.
explanation.walkthrough: Card sharp reads as one phrase for a cheat; split it, Card is the definition and sharp the taste.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarot is one of a pack of cards used in fortune-telling, an example of a card.

clue.text: See 5
The French in their way sent up Swiss polymath

indicators.note: in puts the French article inside the other word
in a down entry, sent up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: rue is French for street, so their way
le is French for the

explanation.surface: The French poke fun at a Swiss genius in their own fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Their refers back to the French, so the way is a French word for road.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was an eighteenth-century Swiss mathematician and physicist, a famous example of a polymath.

clue.text: Tincture team in anger knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means pushed backwards, so the whole thing is reversed
in puts the team inside the word for anger

parts.note: to rile is to anger
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: An angry team downs a medicinal drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Knocked back suggests drinking the tincture, but it signals reversing the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a medicinal solution, often alcohol-based, much like a tincture.

clue.text: Sleep on Pope's instruction: clear?

indicators.note: in an across entry, on places the word for sleep after the other part

parts.note: a papal bull is a formal decree from the Pope
to doze is to sleep lightly

explanation.surface: The Pope orders that everyone sleep: is that clear?
explanation.walkthrough: Clear is the verb to flatten ground with a heavy machine; the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: To bulldoze a site is to flatten and remove everything on it, levelling the land.

clue.text: Tries a drop in house

indicators.note: in places the phrase inside the abbreviation for house

parts.note: HO is an abbreviation for house
taken as written
to sag is to droop or drop

explanation.surface: Somebody attempts a dropped catch indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a go is to make an attempt, so it means tries.

clue.text: Southern woman's club: Notts Forest

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
her is the possessive for a woman
a wood is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A southern woman's football club is Nottingham Forest.
explanation.walkthrough: Notts Forest looks like the football club Nottingham Forest; read literally it is a forest in Nottinghamshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherwood is the ancient royal woodland in Nottinghamshire, home of Robin Hood.
